Thanks Marissa — useful recap. A few clarifications from our engineering team: 

1) Chat vs completions: we plan to use chat for multi-turn UI flows (agent-assist) and completions for single-shot generation in pipelines. Is there a recommended way to switch schemas so our downstream parsers can be deterministic?

2) Tokenization and max_tokens: we need guidance on how to budget tokens across prompt + response. Our typical prompts are ~1.2k tokens and we expect responses up to ~800 tokens at peak (rare).

3) Streaming semantics: for the UI we want partial tokens as they arrive but also a final structured JSON payload (tool-calling) that our worker will consume. How do you recommend reconciling streaming chunks with json-structured output?

4) Auth: for server-side we prefer short-lived keys + a KMS-backed rotation. For console/admin access we use SSO (SAML/OIDC). Any blocking constraints?

If you can send examples for 1-3 that would be great. Happy to hop on a quick 20m tomorrow.

—Alex

Thanks — will answer inline below and loop in Vivek with examples.

Quick answers / recommendations:
- Chat vs Completions schema: use the chat API for multi-turn exchanges and adopt a stable response wrapper (we call it "resultEnvelope") around model output. The envelope includes metadata (model, tokens_used, request_id) and a payload field which contains either plain text or a structured object. This lets your downstream parsers always expect the envelope shape while payload can vary by use case. See attached rsp-schema-examples.json for a template.

- Token budgeting: for 1.2k prompt + 800 response peak you should provision max_tokens >= 900 and set a hard cap. We typically recommend: model selection first (a 32k context model would be ideal), set max_tokens to 1600 as an upper bound for peak cases, and use stop sequences plus token-level safety checks to avoid runaway generation. Also consider prefix caching for repeated system content to save tokens.

- Streaming + structured output: two options:
  1) Evented streaming: stream incremental text deltas to the client for UX while simultaneously emitting a separate final "structured object" event when the model finishes tool-calling/JSON output. Your worker subscribes to the structured event for downstream processing.
  2) Deterministic streaming markers: stream tokens but include a canonical marker (e.g., "<JSON_START>...<JSON_END>") in the stream and validate/parse on the client once the end marker is received. We prefer option 1 for reliability and to avoid partial-JSON parsing on the client.

- Auth: short-lived server keys + KMS rotation are fully supported. For admin console SSO we support SAML/OIDC; we can also federate SCIM for user sync. No blocking constraints.

Vivek — can you attach a minimal SDK example showing streaming + final structured event and a small embeddings->reranker snippet?

Alex — I'll also schedule a follow-up 20m slot if you'd like to walk through the examples live.

Best,
Marissa
